summary: Iter23 — Verified the two new Aarti Sync additions in BhaktiEditorDrawer: (a) Download Current Sync button with correct filename pattern + disabled state, and (b) Confirm Overwrite Sync modal with Cancel / backdrop / invalid-JSON guard / no-existing-sync paths. All 8 sub-tests passed. The saved Hindi sync was NOT mutated — every confirmation path used Cancel/backdrop/invalid-JSON so no POST /sync fired during the run.
verified_behaviours: Login → /admin/arti-manager → edit-item-69f1e1a77488457efddb02b7 opens drawer and Audio Sync tab loads with non-empty JSON containing `verses` key.

Download button (aarti-sync-download-hi) triggered a browser download with suggested filename `Shri_Ganesh_Aarti_hi_sync.json` — matches pattern `*_hi_sync.json`. Saved file parses as valid JSON and contains `verses` (1 verse — the iter22 Test fixture).
Status banner '✓ Downloaded Shri_Ganesh_Aarti_hi_sync.json' renders after click (verified visually in screenshot).
Download button becomes disabled when editor textarea is cleared (disabled attribute set).
Save Sync (aarti-sync-save-hi) with existing sync opens `aarti-sync-confirm-modal-hi` containing the text 'Overwrite existing sync?'.
Cancel button closes the modal, no POST /sync fires, Save button is NOT stuck in saving/spinner state.
Clicking the backdrop of the modal closes it and no POST /sync fires.
Invalid JSON `{not json` → modal is NOT opened, inline error `Invalid JSON: Expected property name or '}' …` is rendered, no POST /sync fires.
Switching language to Marathi (mr) — no existing sync — Save path does NOT open the confirm modal (hasExistingSync=false). Used invalid JSON to avoid any actual save, confirmed 0 POST /sync.
No console errors. No React error overlay. Download icon / Blob download / modal portal all integrate cleanly.
critical_code_review_comments: BhaktiEditorDrawer.js is now 1829 lines — already flagged historically; consider splitting into per-tab modules (AartiSyncTab, AartiAudioTab, AartiVideoTab, AartiThumbTab) to stay under the 700-line guideline. Not blocking for this iter.

handleDownload filename sanitizer regex `/[^\w\u0900-\u097F\-]+/g` correctly preserves Devanagari + word chars and dashes; tested title 'श्री गणेशजी की आरती' transliterated via `title_en` to 'Shri_Ganesh_Aarti' which is fine. If title_en is ever missing and only Devanagari is present, filename like `श्री_गणेशजी_की_आरती_hi_sync.json` would be used — some filesystems/browsers may not handle that gracefully, but it is an acceptable graceful-degrade path.
parseErr is cleared inside requestSave before the hasExistingSync branch, but the `save()` helper also re-validates JSON and clears parseErr — slight duplication, harmless.
seed_data_creation: None. Critically, Hindi sync was NOT overwritten — every confirm path used Cancel/backdrop or Invalid JSON to avoid POST /sync. User can safely restore original 5-verse Hindi sync as planned.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Both new features in AartiSyncTab are fully functional with correct data-testid coverage (aarti-sync-download-<lang>, aarti-sync-save-<lang>, aarti-sync-confirm-modal-<lang>, aarti-sync-confirm-cancel-<lang>, aarti-sync-confirm-ok-<lang>). The 'Overwrite' OK button (aarti-sync-confirm-ok-<lang>) path was NOT clicked during this run (to preserve existing Hindi sync). If a future iter needs to validate the actual overwrite POST, use a throwaway language bucket or explicitly allow mutation.
rca_of_the_issue: n/a — this was a feature-addition verification iter, no bugs found.
